title: Rulebook action type (mechanics/actions/<slug>.json)
description: What an actor (self and / or an entity) can do: parameters, the abstract adapter action it maps to, precondition, duration, motion, effects with mutually exclusive outcomes, cost and cooldown (spec/feature/rulebook.md §3). The visible definition is complete on its own; a .masked.json companion may replace whole keys of it for the omniscient view only.

actor.description: Who can take the action. Only actions with self are the player's own affordances.

maps_to.description: The abstract adapter action (one verb of replay.schema.json#/$defs/action, plus optional target / params). Operands are $params, IDs, node IDs or numbers; validate V16 checks the vocabulary.

duration.description: Seconds (turns in a turn-based game); default 0.

cost.description: Resources the action consumes (variable -> amount, expr/2), read by planners as the cost.

cooldown.description: Seconds before the actor may take the action again.

effects_known.description: false: the action is publicly known to exist but its effects are not modelled (declared on the public side on its own, never derived from a masked file).

where.description: Candidate filter (entity kind), with the candidate bound to the parameter.

step.description: Discretisation step of a number parameter (the planners' only view of a continuous space).

motion.description: Motion primitive the forward model integrates over sub-steps.

kind.description: toward / away / sideways / to_node / hold, or a $param holding one of them.

goal.description: What the motion is relative to: a $param, an ID token or a node.

keep.description: Do not come closer than this (expr/2).

of.description: Owner of the assigned variable: actor, self, a $param or an ID token (none for world / stage variables).

effect.description: One draw: exactly one of `outcomes` happens (they are mutually exclusive and their p add up to 1); the assignments of that outcome happen together. Independent draws are separate effects.

at.description: When the effect applies: at the start, at the end, or this many seconds after the start.
